我在当前基线已经支持 claim 与 path 叶子、equals、in、contains、contains_any、exists、顺序比较以及 all、any、not 组合的基础上，为 POST /v1/policies 的规则增加 claim 或 path 与 contains_all 组成的叶子，表达被定位的数组必须完整覆盖给定候选集合。候选是 1 到 32 个 JSON 标量，按现有严格标量相等语义不得重复，例如 1 与 1.0 重复，而 1 与 true 不重复。既有规则、版本递增、幂等创建、旧版本保留和查询返回顺序不变。

求值时，被定位值必须本身是 JSON 数组，且每个候选项都能在其中找到至少一个严格相等的标量元素；元素顺序、额外元素和重复元素不影响结果，候选不要求相邻。元素与候选项继续严格区分 null、布尔值、字符串和数值，数值按数值大小比较。claim 叶子读取顶层声明值，path 叶子沿用字符串段、通配段和多候选展开；某个完整 path 候选满足 contains_all 时叶子为真，缺失、空数组、非数组、缺少任一候选或类型不匹配均为假。叶子放进 all、any、not 后沿用短路和取反语义，POST /v1/policies/{policy_id}/evaluate 对同一声明重复返回相同 allowed 或 denied，POST /v1/evidence/{evidence_id}/decisions 使用同一语义形成固定状态。

POST /v1/policies 收到空或超过 32 个候选、非列表、非标量、重复候选、contains_all 与其他比较键并存，或定位形状不符合现有约束时返回 422，不分配版本且不写状态。新增比较进入规范化规则 JSON、策略查询、比较差异、决策 trace 和决策 evaluation 的完整叶子解释；解释仍只含节点位置、节点类型与布尔结果，不含声明名、路径、候选项或声明值。旧策略版本、既有比较、通配路径、策略评估、证明决策、审计、幂等并发和重启持久化保持兼容，旧规则不得产生不同结论。

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

1	"""Versioned release-policy rule trees.
2	
3	A rule is a small JSON tree. Leaf nodes locate a value with a top-level
4	claim name or an object path and carry exactly one comparison key::
5	
6	    {"claim": "<top-level claim name>", "equals": <scalar>}
7	    {"path": ["<segment>", ...], "equals": <scalar>}
8	    {"path": ["items", {"wildcard": True}, "id"], "equals": <scalar>}
9	    {"claim": "...", "in": [<scalar>, ...]}        # 1..32 unique scalars
10	    {"claim": "...", "contains": <scalar>}          # array has an equal element
11	    {"claim": "...", "contains_any": [<scalar>, ...]}  # array hits >=1 of 1..32
12	    {"claim": "...", "lt"|"lte"|"gt"|"gte": <finite JSON number>}
13	    {"claim": "...", "exists": true}
14	    {"path": [...], "in"|"contains"|"contains_any"|"lt"|"lte"|"gt"|"gte"|"exists": ...}
15	    {"all": [rule, ...]}
16	    {"any": [rule, ...]}
17	    {"not": rule}
18	
19	A path segment is either a string naming one object field or the exact
20	object ``{"wildcard": True}`` (no other keys, and the value must be the
21	JSON boolean ``true``). A wildcard segment expands every element of the
22	JSON array at that position; several wildcards expand left to right into
23	the full set of candidate paths. A leaf is true when any complete
24	candidate satisfies its comparison.
25	
26	Scalars are JSON scalars (string, number, boolean or null). Rules mention
27	only claim *names* (or object paths) and expected scalar values — they
28	never contain raw evidence, nonces or claim material — so persisting
29	their canonical serialization is compatible with the no-raw-evidence
30	guarantee.
31	"""
32	
33	from __future__ import annotations
34	
35	import json
36	import math
37	from typing import Any
38	
39	__all__ = [
40	    "InvalidRule",
41	    "validate_rule",
42	    "evaluate_rule",
43	    "explain_rule",
44	    "rule_structure",
45	    "rules_equal",
46	    "diff_rules",
47	    "canonical_rule_json",
48	    "MAX_RULE_DEPTH",
49	    "MAX_RULE_NODES",
50	    "MAX_PATH_SEGMENTS",
51	    "MAX_PATH_SEGMENT_LENGTH",
52	    "MAX_IN_ITEMS",
53	]
54	
55	#: Defensive bounds so a submitted rule cannot exhaust the stack or the
56	#: evaluator regardless of nesting.
57	MAX_RULE_DEPTH = 32
58	MAX_RULE_NODES = 256
59	
60	#: Bounds on declared object paths so an unbounded path can never enter
61	#: persisted state.
62	MAX_PATH_SEGMENTS = 8
63	MAX_PATH_SEGMENT_LENGTH = 128
64	
65	#: Bound on the candidate set of an ``in`` or ``contains_any`` leaf so an
66	#: unbounded set can never enter persisted state.
67	MAX_IN_ITEMS = 32
68	
69	#: The comparison keys a leaf may carry exactly one of, next to its
70	#: ``claim``/``path`` locator.
71	_COMPARISON_KEYS = frozenset(
72	    {"equals", "in", "contains", "contains_any", "lt", "lte", "gt", "gte",
73	     "exists"}
74	)
75	
76	#: Comparison keys that order the actual value against one JSON number.
77	_ORDER_KEYS = frozenset({"lt", "lte", "gt", "gte"})
78	
79	#: The locator keys a leaf may carry exactly one of.
80	_LOCATOR_KEYS = frozenset({"claim", "path"})
81	
82	
83	class InvalidRule(ValueError):
84	    """Raised when a submitted rule tree is not one of the valid forms."""
85	
86	
87	def _is_scalar(value: Any) -> bool:
88	    if value is None or isinstance(value, (str, bool, int)):
89	        return True
90	    if isinstance(value, float):
91	        # Reject NaN/Infinity: they are not valid JSON values and would not
92	        # round-trip through the persisted canonical serialization.
93	        return math.isfinite(value)
94	    return False
95	
96	
97	def _is_number(value: Any) -> bool:
98	    """True for a finite JSON number — booleans are never numbers."""
99	    if isinstance(value, bool):
100	        return False
101	    if isinstance(value, int):
102	        return True
103	    if isinstance(value, float):
104	        return math.isfinite(value)
105	    return False
106	
107	
108	def _is_wildcard_segment(segment: Any) -> bool:
109	    """True only for the exact wildcard object ``{"wildcard": True}``.
110	
111	    The object must carry the single key ``wildcard`` whose value is the
112	    JSON boolean ``true``: any other key, any other value type (including
113	    ``1``) or an empty object is a malformed segment, not a wildcard.
114	    """
115	    return (
116	        isinstance(segment, dict)
117	        and len(segment) == 1
118	        and segment.get("wildcard") is True
119	    )
120	
121	
122	def _validate_path(path: Any) -> None:
123	    """Validate the ``path`` sibling of a path leaf.
124	
125	    It must be a non-empty list of at most :data:`MAX_PATH_SEGMENTS`
126	    segments; each segment is either a non-blank string no longer than
127	    :data:`MAX_PATH_SEGMENT_LENGTH` characters, or the exact wildcard
128	    object ``{"wildcard": True}``. A string segment names exactly one
129	    object field — dots embedded in a segment are literal characters of
130	    that single name and never split it, and the literal string ``"*"``
131	    is an ordinary field name. A wildcard segment expands the elements of
132	    the JSON array found at that position.
133	    """
134	    if not isinstance(path, list) or not path:
135	        raise InvalidRule("path must be a non-empty list of segments")
136	    if len(path) > MAX_PATH_SEGMENTS:
137	        raise InvalidRule(f"path may name at most {MAX_PATH_SEGMENTS} segments")
138	    for segment in path:
139	        if _is_wildcard_segment(segment):
140	            continue
141	        if not isinstance(segment, str) or not segment or not segment.strip():
142	            raise InvalidRule(
143	                "path segments must be non-empty strings or "
144	                '{"wildcard": true} objects'
145	            )
146	        if len(segment) > MAX_PATH_SEGMENT_LENGTH:
147	            raise InvalidRule(
148	                f"path segments may be at most {MAX_PATH_SEGMENT_LENGTH} "
149	                "characters"
150	            )
151	
152	
153	def _scalar_equals(actual: Any, expected: Any) -> bool:
154	    """Type-strict JSON scalar equality.
155	
156	    JSON distinguishes ``true`` from ``1`` even though Python does not, and
157	    ``null`` only equals ``null``; numbers of either width compare by value.
158	    """
159	    if actual is None or expected is None:
160	        return actual is None and expected is None
161	    if isinstance(actual, bool) or isinstance(expected, bool):
162	        return (
163	            isinstance(actual, bool)
164	            and isinstance(expected, bool)
165	            and actual == expected
166	        )
167	    if isinstance(actual, str) or isinstance(expected, str):
168	        return (
169	            isinstance(actual, str)
170	            and isinstance(expected, str)
171	            and actual == expected
172	        )
173	    if isinstance(actual, (int, float)) and isinstance(expected, (int, float)):
174	        return actual == expected
175	    return False
176	
177	
178	def _validate_scalar_candidates(key: str, value: Any) -> None:
179	    """Validate a 1..32 list of unique scalars for ``in``/``contains_any``.
180	
181	    Candidates must not repeat under the same type-strict equality the
182	    evaluator applies: 1 and 1.0 repeat, 1 and true do not.
183	    """
184	    if not isinstance(value, list) or not value:
185	        raise InvalidRule(f"{key} must be a non-empty list of scalars")
186	    if len(value) > MAX_IN_ITEMS:
187	        raise InvalidRule(f"{key} may name at most {MAX_IN_ITEMS} candidates")
188	    for item in value:
189	        if not _is_scalar(item):
190	            raise InvalidRule(f"{key} candidates must be scalars")
191	    for index in range(len(value)):
192	        for earlier in value[:index]:
193	            if _scalar_equals(value[index], earlier):
194	                raise InvalidRule(f"{key} candidates must not repeat")
195	
196	
197	def _validate_comparison(key: str, value: Any) -> None:
198	    """Validate the comparison value of a leaf against its comparison key."""
199	    if key == "equals":
200	        if not _is_scalar(value):
201	            raise InvalidRule("equals must compare against a scalar")
202	        return
203	    if key == "contains":
204	        # Only a scalar may be sought in an array: the membership test is
205	        # the same type-strict scalar equality ``equals`` applies.
206	        if not _is_scalar(value):
207	            raise InvalidRule("contains must compare against a scalar")
208	        return
209	    if key in ("in", "contains_any"):
210	        _validate_scalar_candidates(key, value)
211	        return
212	    if key in _ORDER_KEYS:
213	        if not _is_number(value):
214	            raise InvalidRule(f"{key} must compare against a finite JSON number")
215	        return
216	    if key == "exists":
217	        if value is not True:
218	            raise InvalidRule("exists must be true")
219	        return
220	    raise InvalidRule(f"unknown comparison: {key}")
221	
222	
223	def validate_rule(rule: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
224	    """Validate a rule tree, returning it unchanged on success.
225	
226	    Raises :class:`InvalidRule` for anything that is not exactly one of the
227	    documented forms: unknown node keys, multiple/unknown keys on a node,
228	    missing siblings, non-scalar comparisons, malformed ``in`` or
229	    ``contains_any`` sets (empty, oversized, non-scalar or repeating), a
230	    non-scalar ``contains`` target, boolean or non-finite
231	    ordinal bounds, an ``exists`` value other than ``true``, empty
232	    ``all``/``any`` lists, malformed ``path`` siblings (including an
233	    object segment that is not exactly ``{"wildcard": True}``), or
234	    structures past the defensive size bounds.
235	    """
236	    nodes = 0
237	
238	    def visit(node: Any, depth: int) -> None:
239	        nonlocal nodes
240	        if depth > MAX_RULE_DEPTH:
241	            raise InvalidRule("rule nesting too deep")
242	        if not isinstance(node, dict):
243	            raise InvalidRule("rule node must be an object")
244	        keys = set(node.keys())
245	        if not keys:
246	            raise InvalidRule("rule node must not be empty")
247	        nodes += 1
248	        if nodes > MAX_RULE_NODES:
249	            raise InvalidRule("rule too large")
250	        locators = keys & _LOCATOR_KEYS
251	        comparisons = keys & _COMPARISON_KEYS
252	        if len(keys) == 2 and len(locators) == 1 and len(comparisons) == 1:
253	            if "claim" in locators:
254	                claim = node["claim"]
255	                if not isinstance(claim, str) or not claim:
256	                    raise InvalidRule("claim must name a top-level claim")
257	            else:
258	                _validate_path(node["path"])
259	            (comparison,) = comparisons
260	            _validate_comparison(comparison, node[comparison])
261	            return
262	        if len(keys) != 1:
263	            raise InvalidRule("rule node must have exactly one form")
264	        (key,) = keys
265	        if key in ("all", "any"):
266	            children = node[key]
267	            if not isinstance(children, list) or not children:
268	                raise InvalidRule(f"{key} must be a non-empty list of rules")
269	            for child in children:
270	                visit(child, depth + 1)
271	            return
272	        if key == "not":
273	            visit(node[key], depth + 1)
274	            return
275	        raise InvalidRule(f"unknown rule form: {key}")
276	
277	    visit(rule, 0)
278	    return rule
279

"""Tests for the ``contains_any`` array-membership rule leaf.

Covers POST /v1/policies validation (422 with no version allocated and
no effect on a later creation of the same name), canonical persistence
and snapshot rendering, decision evaluation of the new leaf against
verified evidence claims (type-strict scalar equality of array elements
against the candidate set), composition with all/any/not and the other
comparison keys, wildcard paths, the read-only evaluate endpoint, the
compare endpoint's leaf-change detection, explanation shape, and the
unchanged decision boundary codes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import hmac
import json

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from proof_release.app import create_app
from proof_release.db import (
    AuditEvent,
    Decision,
    DecisionEvaluationNode,
    Evidence,
    Policy,
    PolicyCommitCounter,
    PolicyIdempotencyRecord,
    ProofLifecycleEvent,
)
from proof_release.policies import evaluate_rule, explain_rule, rule_structure

TENANT = "tenant-a"
WORKLOAD = "workload-1"
SECRET = "unit-test-secret"

WILD = {"wildcard": True}


@pytest.fixture()
def app(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("PROOF_RELEASE_ATTESTED_NONCE_SECRET", SECRET)
    return create_app(f"sqlite:///{tmp_path}/contains_any.db")


@pytest.fixture()
def client(app):
    return TestClient(app)


def _mac(nonce: str, claims: dict) -> str:
    key = hmac.new(
        SECRET.encode("utf-8"),
        f"{TENANT}:{WORKLOAD}".encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).digest()
    payload = json.dumps(
        {"claims": claims, "nonce": nonce},
        sort_keys=True,
        separators=(",", ":"),
    ).encode("utf-8")
    return hmac.new(key, payload, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


def _evidence(nonce: str, claims: dict) -> str:
    return json.dumps({"nonce": nonce, "claims": claims, "mac": _mac(nonce, claims)})


def _receive_and_verify(client, claims):
    created = client.post(
        "/v1/challenges",
        json={"tenant_id": TENANT, "workload_id": WORKLOAD},
    ).json()
    evidence = _evidence(created["nonce"], claims)
    submitted = client.post(
        "/v1/evidence",
        json={
            "tenant_id": TENANT,
            "workload_id": WORKLOAD,
            "challenge_id": created["challenge_id"],
            "nonce": created["nonce"],
            "evidence_format": "attested-nonce-json",
            "evidence": evidence,
        },
    )
    assert submitted.status_code == 201
    evidence_id = submitted.json()["evidence_id"]
    verified = client.post(
        f"/v1/evidence/{evidence_id}/verify",
        json={
            "tenant_id": TENANT,
            "workload_id": WORKLOAD,
            "nonce": created["nonce"],
            "evidence": evidence,
        },
    )
    assert verified.status_code == 200
    assert verified.json()["status"] == "verified"
    return created, evidence, evidence_id


def _policy(client, rule, name="release", **overrides):
    body = {
        "tenant_id": TENANT,
        "workload_id": WORKLOAD,
        "name": name,
        "rule": rule,
    }
    body.update(overrides)
    return client.post("/v1/policies", json=body)


def _create_policy(client, rule, name="release", **overrides):
    response = _policy(client, rule, name=name, **overrides)
    assert response.status_code == 201
    return response.json()


def _decide(client, evidence_id, created, evidence, policy_id, **overrides):
    body = {
        "tenant_id": TENANT,
        "workload_id": WORKLOAD,
        "nonce": created["nonce"],
        "evidence": evidence,
        "policy_id": policy_id,
    }
    body.update(overrides)
    return client.post(f"/v1/evidence/{evidence_id}/decisions", json=body)


def _status_for(client, claims, rule, name="release"):
    created, evidence, evidence_id = _receive_and_verify(client, claims)
    policy = _create_policy(client, rule, name=name)
    response = _decide(client, evidence_id, created, evidence, policy["policy_id"])
    assert response.status_code == 200
    return response.json()["status"]


def _evaluate(client, policy_id, claims, **overrides):
    body = {
        "tenant_id": TENANT,
        "workload_id": WORKLOAD,
        "claims": claims,
    }
    body.update(overrides)
    return client.post(f"/v1/policies/{policy_id}/evaluate", json=body)


def _compare(client, left_policy_id, right_policy_id):
    return client.get(
        "/v1/policies/compare",
        params={
            "tenant_id": TENANT,
            "workload_id": WORKLOAD,
            "left_policy_id": left_policy_id,
            "right_policy_id": right_policy_id,
        },
    )


# --- pure semantics --------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "actual,candidates",
    [
        (["gold", "silver"], ["gold"]),
        (["gold", "silver"], ["platinum", "silver"]),
        ([1, 2, 3], [2]),
        ([1, 2, 3], [9, 2.0]),
        ([1.0, 2.0], [1]),
        ([-0.0], [0]),
        ([True, False], [False]),
        ([None, "x"], [None]),
        (["x", None, 1], [None, "missing"]),
        # Objects/arrays among the elements do not disturb the scan.
        (["a", {"k": "v"}, ["nested"], 1], [1]),
        # Several candidates of mixed scalar types.
        (["b"], ["a", "b", "c"]),
        ([3], ["a", None, True, 3]),
    ],
)
def test_contains_any_pure_match(actual, candidates):
    assert evaluate_rule(
        {"claim": "a", "contains_any": candidates}, {"a": actual}
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "actual,candidates",
    [
        # Empty, non-array, absent-shaped values.
        ([], ["x"]),
        ("gold", ["gold"]),
        (1, [1]),
        (True, [True]),
        (None, [None]),
        ({"gold": 1}, ["gold"]),
        # Type-strict misses: true is not 1, numeric strings are not
        # numbers, null only equals null.
        ([1], [True]),
        ([True], [1]),
        (["2"], [2]),
        ([2], ["2"]),
        ([0], [False]),
        ([False], [0]),
        ([None], [False, 0, ""]),
        ([""], [None]),
        # Non-scalar elements never equal a scalar candidate.
        ([["gold"]], ["gold"]),
        ([{"x": 1}], [1]),
        # No candidate matches any element.
        (["gold", "silver"], ["platinum", "bronze"]),
    ],
)
def test_contains_any_pure_miss(actual, candidates):
    assert not evaluate_rule(
        {"claim": "a", "contains_any": candidates}, {"a": actual}
    )


def test_contains_any_pure_missing_claim_and_path():
    assert not evaluate_rule(
        {"claim": "a", "contains_any": [1]}, {"other": [1]}
    )
    assert not evaluate_rule(
        {"path": ["t", "tags"], "contains_any": [1]}, {"t": {}}
    )
    # A non-object on the descent path is a miss, not an error.
    assert not evaluate_rule(
        {"path": ["t", "tags"], "contains_any": [1]}, {"t": ["x"]}
    )
    # A terminal array under a path matches element-wise.
    assert evaluate_rule(
        {"path": ["t", "tags"], "contains_any": [1, 2]},
        {"t": {"tags": [1, 2]}},
    )


def test_contains_any_pure_wildcard_any_candidate_hits():
    rule = {"path": ["items", WILD, "tags"], "contains_any": ["x", "y"]}
    claims = {"items": [{"tags": ["a"]}, {"tags": ["y"]}]}

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "actual,candidates",
    [
        # Empty, non-array, absent-shaped values.
        ([], ["x"]),
        ("gold", ["gold"]),
        (1, [1]),
        (True, [True]),
        (None, [None]),
        ({"gold": 1}, ["gold"]),
        # One candidate short.
        (["gold"], ["gold", "silver"]),
        (["gold", "bronze"], ["gold", "silver"]),
        # Type-strict misses: true is not 1, numeric strings are not
        # numbers, null only equals null.
        ([1], [1, True]),
        ([True], [True, 1]),
        (["2"], [2, "2"]),
        ([2], [2, "2"]),
        ([0], [0, False]),
        ([False], [0, False]),
        ([None, False, 0, ""], [None, ""]),
        ([""], [None, ""]),
        # Non-scalar elements never equal a scalar candidate.
        ([["gold"]], ["gold"]),
        ([{"x": 1}], [1]),
        ([["gold"], "silver"], ["gold", "silver"]),
        # Repeats in the array do not cover distinct candidates.
        (["gold", "gold"], ["gold", "silver"]),
        ([1, 1], [1, 1.0]),  # 1 and 1.0 are the SAME candidate: covered.
    ],
)
def test_contains_all_pure_miss_or_match(actual, candidates):
    # The parametrize table above mixes outcomes: compute the expected
    # result with an explicit, independent subset definition so a failure
    # names the exact pair.
    result = evaluate_rule(
        {"claim": "a", "contains_all": candidates}, {"a": actual}
    )
    if not isinstance(actual, list):
        assert result is False
        return
    expected = all(
        any(
            type(element) is not bool
            and not isinstance(element, (dict, list))
            and _loose_scalar_equal(element, candidate)
            for element in actual
        )
        for candidate in candidates
    )
    assert result is expected


def _loose_scalar_equal(left, right):
    # Mirror of policies._scalar_equals without importing the private name.
    if left is None or right is None:
        return left is None and right is None
    if isinstance(left, bool) or isinstance(right, bool):
        return isinstance(left, bool) and isinstance(right, bool) and left == right
    if isinstance(left, str) or isinstance(right, str):
        return isinstance(left, str) and isinstance(right, str) and left == right
    if isinstance(left, (int, float)) and isinstance(right, (int, float)):
        return left == right
    return False

from __future__ import annotations

import hmac
import json

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from proof_release.app import create_app
from proof_release.db import (

)

WORKLOAD = "workload-1"
SECRET = "unit-test-secret"

def _mac(nonce: str, claims: dict) -> str:

        SECRET.encode("utf-8"),
        f"{TENANT}:{WORKLOAD}".encode("utf-8"),

    ).digest()
    payload = json.dumps(
        {"claims": claims, "nonce": nonce},
        sort_keys=True,
        separators=(",", ":"),
    ).encode("utf-8")
    return hmac.new(key, payload, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


def _evidence(nonce: str, claims: dict) -> str:

def _receive_and_verify(client, claims):

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "actual,candidates",

        (["silver", "gold"], ["gold", "silver"]),
        # Extra elements do not matter.
        (["a", "b", "c"], ["a", "c"]),
        (["a", "b", "c"], ["c"]),
        # Repeated elements do not matter.
        (["a", "a", "b"], ["a", "b"]),
        # Candidates need not be adjacent.
        ([1, 2, 3, 4], [1, 4]),
        ([1, 2, 3], [3, 1]),
        # A single candidate behaves like membership.
        (["gold", "silver"], ["gold"]),
        ([1, 2, 3], [2]),
        # Numeric equality by value.
        ([1.0, 2.0], [1, 2]),
        ([-0.0, 1], [0]),
        # 1 and true are distinct; with both present the set is covered.
        ([True, 1], [1, True]),
        ([False, 0], [0, False]),
        # Null among the elements.
        ([None, "x"], [None, "x"]),
        # Objects/arrays among the elements do not disturb the scan.
        (["a", {"k": "v"}, ["nested"], 1], [1, "a"]),
        # Mixed scalar types in the candidate set.
        ([3, "a", None, True], ["a", None, True, 3]),
        # The 32-candidate boundary, fully covered.

        # The array may be far larger than the candidate set.

        {"claim": "a", "contains_all": candidates}, {"a": actual}

    "actual,candidates",

        ("gold", ["gold"]),
        (1, [1]),
        (True, [True]),
        (None, [None]),
        ({"gold": 1}, ["gold"]),

        (["gold"], ["gold", "silver"]),
        (["gold", "bronze"], ["gold", "silver"]),
        # Type-strict misses: true is not 1, numeric strings are not
        # numbers, null only equals null.
        ([1], [1, True]),
        ([True], [True, 1]),
        (["2"], [2, "2"]),
        ([2], [2, "2"]),
        ([0], [0, False]),
        ([False], [0, False]),
        ([None, False, 0, ""], [None, ""]),
        ([""], [None, ""]),

    expected = all(

    if isinstance(left, bool) or isinstance(right, bool):

    if isinstance(left, str) or isinstance(right, str):
        return isinstance(left, str) and isinstance(right, str) and left == right
